# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 69

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — Opening frame: "after seeing all of this" vs. "after I had seen all these things"

- **EMET:** "After all these things I said to him"
- **LOGOS:** "After I had seen all these things, I said to him"
- **PNEUMA:** "After seeing all of this I said"
- **Greek:** *meta tauta panta* — "after all these things"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "After I had seen all these things I asked him" (LOGOS). The explicit subject and past perfect improve readability without losing fidelity.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "benefits them" vs. "profits them" for repentance's result

- **EMET:** "does their repentance profit them?"
- **LOGOS:** "does their repentance benefit them before the Lord?"
- **PNEUMA:** "does it actually benefit them? Does it get them life before the Lord?"
- **Greek:** *ōphelei autous hē metanoia* — "does repentance benefit/profit them"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "does their repentance benefit them? Does it give them life before the Lord?" (LOGOS). "Benefit" is clearer than "profit" in modern usage; PNEUMA's split into two questions is a helpful clarification adopted in part.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "cleanse" vs. "purge" vs. "cleanse themselves"

- **EMET:** "cleanse themselves from all wickedness"
- **LOGOS:** "cleanse themselves from all the evil things"
- **PNEUMA:** "cleanses themselves from all the evil I described"
- **Greek:** *katharisōsin heautous apo pasōn tōn ponēriōn* — "cleanse themselves from all the evil deeds"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "cleanse themselves from all the evil things I described" (PNEUMA). The added referential phrase "I described" echoes the narrative context well.

---

## Disagreement 4 — "double-minded" vs. "wavering" in 69:1

- **EMET:** "do not become double-minded about the commandments"
- **LOGOS:** "do not waver with regard to the commandments"
- **PNEUMA:** "double-minded about the commandments"
- **Greek:** *dipsychēsōsin peri tōn entolōn* — "be double-minded/vacillating about the commandments"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "double-minded concerning the commandments" (EMET/PNEUMA). *Dipsychia* is a technical term in Hermas and should be preserved as "double-minded" throughout.

---

## Disagreement 5 — "abandon themselves to desires" vs. "indulging themselves"

- **EMET:** "who give themselves over to their desires"
- **LOGOS:** "who deliver themselves to their own desires"
- **PNEUMA:** "keep indulging themselves"
- **Greek:** *paradidōsin heautous tais epithymiais autōn* — "hand themselves over to their desires"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "who abandon themselves to their own desires" (blend). "Abandon themselves" captures the volitional act of self-surrender better than "indulge."

---

## Disagreement 6 — Structure of 69:3 quotation introduction

- **EMET:** "I have heard from certain teachers"
- **LOGOS:** "I have heard from some teachers"
- **PNEUMA:** "I've heard from some teachers"
- **Greek:** *ēkousa apo tinōn didaskalōn* — "I heard from certain teachers"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I have heard from some teachers" (LOGOS). "Some teachers" is more natural than "certain teachers" without loss of meaning.

---

## Disagreement 7 — "go down into the water" vs. "at baptism"

- **EMET:** "when we descended into the water and received forgiveness"
- **LOGOS:** "when we go down into the water and receive forgiveness of our former sins"
- **PNEUMA:** "the forgiveness you receive at baptism"
- **Greek:** *katabainontōn hēmōn eis to hydōr* — "when we go down into the water"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when we go down into the water and receive forgiveness of our former sins" (LOGOS). The Greek phrase should be preserved literally; PNEUMA's "at baptism" is accurate but loses the vivid immersion imagery.

---

## Disagreement 8 — "it is once only" vs. "once and final"

- **EMET:** "it is once only"
- **LOGOS:** "it is once and final"
- **PNEUMA:** "it's once only and final"
- **Greek:** *haplē estin* — "it is single/one" (with contextual implication of finality)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "it is once only and final" (PNEUMA). Both "once only" and "final" are needed to capture both the singularity (*haplē*) and the irreversible character that context demands.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 69:4 closing — "will have difficulty living" vs. "will hardly live"

- **EMET:** "such a person will scarcely live"
- **LOGOS:** "such a one will with difficulty attain life"
- **PNEUMA:** "such a one will have difficulty living"
- **Greek:** *molis zēsetai ho toioutos* — "with difficulty will such a one live"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "such a one will have difficulty living" (PNEUMA). Natural and accurate; preserves the adverb *molis* as a genuine qualifier rather than softening it.

---

*Disagreement log generated 2026-03-17. SOPHIA rulings are binding for the consensus text.*
